title: Causal Observability Hypothesis Lab Guide
author: Asha Kulkarni
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a repeatable lab process for designing, instrumenting, and validating causal hypotheses about runtime behavior. It is intended for engineers and SREs who need to move beyond correlation and produce defensible, actionable conclusions about how runtime subsystems (kernel scheduler, KV cache, request router, model variants) affect SLOs, cost, and fidelity.

Goals
- Provide a minimally invasive experiment framework for production-like workloads.
- Standardize telemetry, experiment matrices, and statistical thresholds.
- Produce runbooks and artifact templates (traces, dashboards, cohort exports) that can be handed to product/ops.

Scope
- Focus: serving runtime subsystems: kernel scheduler, KV cache, batching, model-variant routing, and prefix/sequence handling.
- Not in scope: model architecture changes, upstream customer prompts, and offline training pipelines.

Owners and Roles
1) Lab Owner: eng-serving-runtime / Profiling team (primary contact: Asha Kulkarni).
2) Experiment Lead: engineer running instrumentation and experiment orchestration.
3) Data Owner: Observability team (responsible for query access and retention).
4) Oncall / Escalation: runtime-oncall@redwood (see runbooks for pager steps).

When to use this guide
- Tail-latency spikes correlated with kernel scheduler changes.
- Cost-per-token regressions that coincide with quantization/kernel rollouts.
- Suspected causal link between caching behavior and degraded throughput for specific tenant shapes.

Required telemetry and data products
- High-cardinality traces (span-level): sampler rate >= 1/100 for public prod; full traces for canary.
- Per-request SLI metrics: request_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, tokens_generated, kernel_ms, queue_ms, kvcache_hit(boolean).
- Kernel-level counters: kernel_invoke_ms, kernel_queue_length, occupancy_percent.
- Cost and billing signals: token_cost_estimate_per_request.

Minimal SLOs for experiments
- Baseline SLO: p95 <= 250ms for interactive routes; p99 <= 800ms.
- Canary gating: no >5% relative increase in p95 and no >2x increase in p99 for test groups.

Telemetry table (minimum dataset)
Metric | Source | Retention | SLI mapping
-------|--------|----------|------------
request_latency_ms_p95 | Prometheus + aggregated traces | 90d (raw histograms), 365d (rollup) | p95 latency SLI
tokens_generated | App logs / usage stream | 180d | cost per token derivation
kernel_invoke_ms | kernel telemetry agent | 30d (detailed) | kernel cost attribution
kvcache_hit | runtime logs (structured) | 90d | fidelity/cold-start analysis
trace_id | zipkin/jaeger | 30d | causal trace stitching

Hypothesis design template
1) Hypothesis statement (explicit): e.g., "Enabling cold-cache prefetch reduces p99 latency for short prefix requests by >= 20% for route=/chat-compact".
2) Expected causal mechanism: describe the chain (prefetch -> less KV cache miss -> fewer kernel cold-starts -> lower tail latency).
3) Observable signals: which metrics/spans will change and direction.
4) Minimum detectable effect (MDE): numeric threshold (e.g., 20% reduction at p99).
5) Failure modes and safety checks: e.g., overall throughput drop, token-cost increase > 5%.

Experiment design checklist
- Select cohorts: use tenant hashing or route-based split. Use 10% treatment size for initial runs; scale to 30–50% for power.
- Control for confounders: time-of-day, model-variant, request-size distribution.
- Instrument additional spans: add a short-lived span around kvcache.lookup and kernel.warmup to capture warm paths.
- Set sampling rules: increase trace sampling for affected tenants during experiment window.
- Run synthetic replays (shadow) if safe to reproduce traffic shape.

Statistical rules and significance
- Primary test: two-sample non-parametric test (Mann-Whitney U) on latency percentiles; bootstrap confidence intervals for p99.
- Significance threshold: alpha = 0.05; report two-sided p-values.
- Powering: aim for 80% power to detect the MDE; if not achievable, increase treatment size or test duration.
- Multiple comparisons: control family-wise error rate when testing multiple routes/percentiles using Bonferroni or Benjamini–Hochberg as appropriate.

Instrumentation snippets and commands
- Start a focused trace capture (developer-friendly CLI):
  rwdctl trace start --service runtime-service --filter 'route=/chat-compact and model_variant in (v1,v1-quant)' --sampler 0.1 --output run-\"kv-prefetch-2025-03\"

- Prometheus example queries (copyable):
  p95 latency by route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"runtime-service\"}[5m])) by (le, route))
  kv cache hit rate: sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[5m]))

- Example structured trace span (JSON example, truncated):
  {
    "trace_id": "abcd1234ef",
    "spans": [
      {"name": "kvcache.lookup", "start_ms": 1690000000, "duration_ms": 2, "tags": {"hit": true}},
      {"name": "kernel.invoke", "start_ms": 1690000010, "duration_ms": 14, "tags": {"kernel_name": "cuda-attention-v2"}}
    ]
  }

Hypothesis example: KV-prefetch probe
- Context: a rollout of an adaptive prefetch feature showed mixed latency signals. We need a causal test to prove net tail-latency benefit without cost regressions.
- Hypothesis: adaptive prefetch reduces p99 by >= 15% on short-prefix chat requests while keeping token-cost delta <= +3%.
- Steps:
  1) Canary prefetch on 10% of tenants, instrument additional spans.
  2) Run 7-day experiment (to cover daily cycle) with baseline and treatment cohorts.
  3) Collect traces for treatment and control (increase sampling to 1/20).
  4) Compute bootstrap CI for p99 and test using Mann-Whitney U.
  5) If p-value < 0.05 and effect size >= 15% with cost delta <= 3%, promote to 30% and repeat.

Data artifacts to commit
- Experiment README (short): purpose, hypothesis, dataset keys, queries, dashboards used, failure criteria.
- Trace bundles: path to zipped traces and a small sample of full trace JSONs.
- Notebook: analysis notebook (BigQuery or pandas) with code to compute p95/p99, bootstrap CI, and cost apportionment.
- Dashboard snapshot: Grafana panel JSON or link.

Canary gating and rollout policy (recommended)
1) Preflight: unit tests, microbenchmarks, and synthetic replay on staging.
2) Canary 10% for 48–72 hours with elevated telemetry.
3) Safety checks: no >5% regression on p95 and p99, no >10% increase in kernel invocation rate, token-cost delta <= 3%.
4) If passed, expand to 30% for 3–7 days.
5) If passed, promote to 100% via staged waves with monitoring runbooks active.

Troubleshooting and common pitfalls
- Confounding rollout traffic: model variants or user-agent skews can mimic treatment effects. Always stratify by model_variant and request_size.
- Sampling bias: low sampling can hide tail effects; increase sampling or use targeted full-trace capture for affected tenants.
- Metric cardinality explosion: avoid instrumenting high-cardinality labels for long retention; use sharding keys and aggregate at ingestion.

Safety, privacy, and compliance notes
- Traces may contain prompt tokens; redact or pseudonymize before exporting to notebooks. Follow data-residency policy for customer-sensitive tenants.
- For private deployments, ensure KMS authorization for trace export.

Post-experiment checklist
1) Summarize results (1-page). Include effect sizes, p-values, CI, and cost impact.
2) Runbook update: if behavior changes runtime response patterns, add/update runbook steps.
3) Backfill monitoring: add long-term dashboards for any new spans/metrics.
4) Archive artifacts: notebook, trace bundle, dashboard, and README in the experiments bucket with tagging.

Appendices
A. Experiment matrix template (CSV columns)\- experiment_id, hypothesis_statement, treatment_percent, start_ts, end_ts, route, model_variant_filter, sampling_delta, primary_metric, mde, p_value, owner, artifacts_link
\B. Quick grep commands\- Find traces containing kernel name:
  rwdctl traces grep --contains \"cuda-attention-v2\" run-\"kv-prefetch-2025-03\"
\C. Related pages and references\- Runtime anomaly hypothesis playbook: /eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/runtime-anomaly-hypothesis-and-investigation-patterns-2026\- Telemetry rollup guide: /eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/telemetry-rollup-and-sample-strategies-2026

Contact and feedback
For questions or to propose additions to this lab guide, open a PR in the eng-serving-runtime docs repo and ping #runtime-profiling on Slack.
